title.narrative: NIHR DA 1: A political economy and comparative analysis of the politics and governance of mobility in African cities.

description.narrative:
A low- and middle-income country (LMIC) award led by Makerere University School of Public Health (MakSPH), Uganda in partnership with the University of Rwanda and Kamuzu University of Health Sciences, Malawi, University of Antwerp, Belgium and Canterbury Christ Church University, UK. Together this partnership aims to understand the political and governance dynamics of cities in order to inform mobility planning and contextually adapted strategies in Uganda, Rwanda and Malawi.
In the context of rapid urbanisation, African countries are grappling with how to manage emerging issues such as unplanned transport systems, accessibility challenges, traffic congestion and vehicle accidents. Sustainable Development Goal (SDG) 11 focuses on making cities and human settlements inclusive, safe, resilient and sustainable with its achievement largely influenced by governance, politics and interests that shape how policy decisions are made and implemented. However, such broad health objectives, coupled with complex governance arrangements have received inadequate attention in the area of mobility and road safety within the African region.
Commencing in January 2025, the twelve-month award will draw on diverse methodologies, theoretical frameworks and empirical analyses to generate evidence which will inform a broader research proposal. Capacity enhancement efforts will be cross-cutting and pursued at individual, organisational and partnership levels. Core activities include knowledge generation via analysis of policies and a scoping review on the political factors and dynamics shaping mobility in African cities, coupled with stakeholder and partnership engagement, evidence needs assessments and capacity development. This award will provide opportunities for mutual learning across the partnership, research community and practitioners through a comparative approach, learning by doing, exchanges and embedded capacity-building activities. These insights will inform the development of broader research projects and wider partnerships which are the ultimate outcomes of this award’s activity.

The award has five objectives:
1. To map and characterise the mobility-related policies across relevant sectors and organisations in cities of Kampala (Uganda), Kigali (Rwanda), and Lilongwe (Malawi). 2. To conduct a scoping review on how contextual factors, actor relationships, and power dynamics shape the development and implementation of mobility-related policies in different urban contexts in the wider global context. 3. To engage decision-makers in the identification and understanding of context-specific evidence needs required for policy changes and implementation challenges related to advancing mobility. 4. To develop a partnership to foster capacity enhancement for interdisciplinary social science research on public health policy in select African university settings. 5. To widen partnerships and produce a proposal for a longer-term grant that develops a consortium approach to enhance expertise, knowledge and resources for political analyses, policy advice and influence at partner institutions to support mobility in African cities.
